transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thanks so much for seeing me. I hope it's okay that I'm taking up your time. 

Um, I guess my family thought I should come talk to somebody. It's just... well, usually I'm just a normal crew guy, you know? Just regular landscaping, doing what I'm told. But recently, I kind of... I guess I got a little carried away. I mean, it's good to be motivated, right? But I went from just doing my job to suddenly trying to run three different bids all at once. 

I was calling city people, trying to line up all these wholesale plant suppliers, and... well, I started messaging just about everybody I knew about this big park idea I had. It was just this sudden rush where I felt like I couldn't shut it off, if that makes sense? I hope I'm explaining this right... is that the kind of thing you need to know?
Did you feel unusually happy or euphoric during this period where you were highly motivated?

Well, um, I don't know if I'd say euphoric. That sounds like a big word, you know? But I did feel... fired up. Really good. Almost like I was bigger than myself, like I could handle anything. It felt great, honestly. 

But, um... well, I guess I should mention that I wasn't always just happy. I hate to admit it, but... if one of the other guys on the crew questioned my plan, or told me I needed to slow down, I... I'd kind of snap at them. And, like, way harder than made sense for the situation. I feel terrible about it now. I'm usually really easygoing, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making myself sound like a jerk...
Have you experienced any periods of feeling really down or depressed in the past?

Um, yeah... I guess that's exactly what happened next. I hope it's okay to explain it like this, but... that fired-up, overconfident stretch I was just talking about? It started right when I began, like, totally remaking myself for that big park pitch. And it lasted for about two weeks, where I was just going non-stop. 

But then... well, I crashed. I just felt really, really down after those two weeks were up. I feel bad even admitting it, because I don't want to sound like a complainer or like I'm lazy or anything. I really should be able to just handle things better and push through, you know? But I just hit a wall and felt awful. 

Did I... did I answer your question okay? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Did you experience any strange thoughts or hear voices during those two weeks when you were feeling fired up or after you crashed?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I know I was acting a little intense, but I wasn't... I wasn't crazy or anything. I didn't hear anything that wasn't there, and I didn't think anything weird, just... just that I had really good ideas for work. 

I'm completely normal that way, I promise. I know it probably sounds bad, the way I was acting, but I wasn't out of my mind. I hope you don't think I'm, like, totally losing it? I'm really trying to be honest with you, I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound worse than it was.
Did you have difficulty sleeping during those two weeks when you were feeling fired up?

Um, difficulty sleeping? No, I don't think so. I mean, I was pretty wrapped up in all the landscaping plans for that pitch, but I wasn't, like, tossing and turning or staring at the ceiling or anything like that. When I actually laid down, I slept fine. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a bigger answer for that one... I really want to make sure I'm giving you all the details you need to figure this out. But yeah, my sleep seemed pretty normal to me, I promise. Did I explain that okay?
Did you find yourself needing less rest or having more energy than usual during those two weeks?

Um, well... I guess I did have a lot of energy. I hope it doesn't make me sound manic or out of control, because I was actually being really productive. I just... I didn't feel tired, you know? 

I'd be up way before daylight, loading all the tools into the truck, sketching out new flower beds, pricing out all these native plants... and then I'd work a full day outside. But even after all that, I just felt this... this drive. Like I had to keep going. I didn't really feel like I needed to stop and rest. 

Is it okay that I was working that much? I just really wanted to do a good job on the pitch. I hope that doesn't sound like I was doing something wrong... I was just really focused, I promise. Does that make sense?
Did you engage in any impulsive or reckless behaviors during those two weeks when you were feeling fired up?

Um, reckless? I... I wouldn't say reckless. I really hope you don't think I'm the kind of guy who just goes wild or does bad things. I was just... I guess I got a little carried away with the business side of things. 

I wanted everything to be perfect, so I... well, I put a bunch of new tools, and all those native plants, and some new work clothes on my credit card. I even paid for some ads. I just... I acted like the money from the pitch was already coming in, you know? Like it was a sure thing and I was just investing in myself to do a good job. 

But... um... honestly, I look at the credit card balance now and I just feel sick to my stomach, because I... I can't cover it. I feel really stupid admitting that to you. I'm usually so careful, I promise. I hope you don't think I'm totally irresponsible for doing that... I really thought it was the right move at the time. Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I just don't want you to think badly of me.
How long did you feel really down after you crashed?

Um... well, I hope I don't sound like I'm just whining or complaining, because I know I should be able to just shake it off. But... honestly, that really down feeling? It's kind of been hanging over me for about a year now. 

I mean, I've really tried to keep a good attitude and just do my work, I promise I have. But after that high wore off, this latest crash... it's just the worst it’s gotten. I feel awful even admitting that to you, like I should be stronger or something. 

Is it okay that it's lasted that long? I really want to get back to being reliable and doing a good job, I just... I hope you don't think I'm just giving up or being lazy. Does that make sense?
How often would you say you feel really down like you've been feeling for the past year?

Um... well, honestly? It feels like it's just... always there. Like, almost every day for the past year. 

I really try to put on a brave face, you know? I don't want my clients or anyone to think I'm slacking off. I still show up and try to do the work, I promise I do. But... underneath it all, I just feel so heavy and empty, pretty much all the time. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a burden or like I'm just feeling sorry for myself. I really want to be better. Is it normal to feel this bad for this long? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can help me... I really don't want to be a difficult patient.
Have you ever had a period of feeling really down that lasted less than two weeks?

Um... less than two weeks? I... I don't think so. I mean, when it hits, it really seems to stick around. 

I hope I'm remembering that right. I wouldn't want to mislead you or give you the wrong idea. I just... once I get into that slump, I can't seem to just snap out of it in a few days, even though I really, really try to. I promise I try to just push through it and get back to work. 

But yeah, I don't think I've ever had it just go away quickly like that. Is... is that a bad thing? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for.
Have you noticed any regular pattern or cycle to when you feel really down or really fired up?

Um... a pattern? I... I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed a specific cycle or anything like that. 

I mean, I try not to dwell on it too much, you know? I just try to take each day as it comes and focus on getting my work done. I hope that's okay to say. I just... I haven't really kept track of it like maybe I should have. 

Is there something specific I should be looking out for? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out. I'm sorry I don't have a better answer for you... I hope I'm not making this harder for you.
Do you think your periods of feeling really down or really fired up happen at specific times of the year?

Um... specific times of the year? I... I don't really think so. Working outside all year doing groundskeeping, you'd think I'd notice if it was tied to the weather or the seasons, but... it just sort of happens whenever. 

Like, the heavy feeling, or those times I'm just running on overdrive... they don't really seem to care what month it is. I hope that makes sense. I'm really trying my best to think back, I promise. 

Should I be paying more attention to the calendar? I can definitely start writing the dates down if that would make your job easier... I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Do you usually feel really down after one of those periods where you're feeling fired up and have a lot of energy?

Um... down right after being fired up? I... I don't really think so. Not right away, at least. 

I mean, I don't want to say for sure and be wrong, but it feels like there's usually a break in between. Like, I'll have that time where I'm getting a ton of work done and feeling really good, and then... it just kind of levels out for a while. I just go back to normal, doing my job, trying to stay out of everyone's way. 

Then eventually, yeah, that heavy feeling comes back. But it doesn't feel like one causes the other, you know? I hope that's the right way to explain it. Does that sound like what usually happens to people? I can try to think harder about it if you need me to... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you always crash or feel really down after one of those periods where you're feeling fired up?

Um... always crash? I... I don't think it's an "always" kind of thing. Like I was saying, there's usually a gap. 

I mean, I'm sure I've had times where I felt down after, but it's not like... a rule or anything. Most of the time, the energy just sort of fades out and I'm back to regular me. I just go back to pulling weeds and mowing and doing my regular routine. 

I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just... I don't want to give you the impression that I'm completely out of control, swinging back and forth constantly. I'm usually pretty steady in between. Is that... is that okay? I'm trying to be as accurate as I can for you.
Do you usually feel really down or crashed after one of those periods where you're feeling fired up?

Oh, um... I'm sorry, I must not be explaining myself very well if we're still on this. That's completely my fault. 

Um... no, I really don't think I usually crash right after. Like I was trying to say before, the energy mostly just... fades out, and I go back to feeling pretty normal for a while. I promise I'm not trying to hide it if I do crash, I just... I really don't think they happen back-to-back like that for me. 

I hope I'm not messing up your evaluation by saying that. Am I... am I supposed to be crashing right after? I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me, so if I'm answering this wrong, please just let me know.
Do you usually feel down or crashed at some point after one of those periods where you're feeling fired up?

Oh! Um, yes. At some point later on... yeah, I definitely do. 

I'm so sorry, I think I was just getting too hung up on the "right after" part before. But yes, eventually that really heavy, low feeling always seems to come back around. I'll be doing okay for a bit, just working and keeping my head down, and then... yeah, the bottom just kind of falls out again. It gets pretty hard to keep up with everything when that happens. 

I feel terrible that it took me this long to understand what you were asking. Does that... does that answer it better? I really hope I'm being helpful now.
How often do you have periods where you feel fired up and have a lot of energy like you described earlier?

Um... how often? I... I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. 

I guess I haven't really kept a strict count or anything. It's not like it happens all the time. Just... every now and then, I suppose? I wish I could give you an exact number, I really do. I'm sorry if that's too vague. 

Is it... is it important that I start tracking them? I can definitely try to do that if it would help you figure things out. I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
How long do your periods of feeling fired up and having a lot of energy usually last?

Um... well, the last time it happened, it was when I was trying to, um, remake myself for this big pitch I had for a park project at work. I wanted to impress my boss, you know? So I got really into it, felt super confident... and that lasted for about two weeks, I think? 

And then, um... then I had that crash we were talking about. 

I hope two weeks doesn't sound too crazy. I mean, I was just really focused on doing a good job. Is that... is that a normal amount of time for something like that to last? I really hope I'm giving you the kind of details you need.
How many times have you had a period of feeling fired up like the one you described in the past year?

In the past year? Oh, um... I really couldn't give you an exact number. I'm so sorry. I... I guess I just haven't been keeping track like I probably should have. 

It's definitely not, like, all the time or anything! I promise it's not constantly happening. Mostly I'm just doing my regular landscaping work, trying to keep the properties looking nice, you know? So maybe just... a couple of times? Or a few? I honestly don't know for sure. 

I feel awful that I don't have a better answer for you. Is it... is it really bad that I can't remember exactly how many times? I can try to sit down and map out the whole year if you need me to, I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you think your periods of feeling fired up or really down might be connected to any particular time of year?

Um... time of year? I... I don't think so? 

I mean, my work gets a lot busier in the spring and summer, obviously, with all the planting and mowing and everything. So maybe I'm a little more tired then? But as far as the really high energy or the bad crashes... I haven't really noticed a pattern with the seasons. 

Is that something that usually happens? Like, do people usually get like this in the winter or something? I feel like I should have paid more attention to when these things happen. I'm sorry, I hope it's okay that I don't really have a good answer for that either. I can try to look back at my work schedule and see if anything lines up, if that would be helpful?
